More than 1,300 people are missing in Nepal and Tibet, including 47 Americans, after a glacial collapse caused catastrophic floods, with video showing mud sweeping through entire communities. Drone footage in Nepal showed roads destroyed and buildings buried by thundering water the color of wet cement. Nepalese authorities ramped up operations in the worst-affected districts of Nuwakot and Rasuwa. The disaster in Nepal and Tibet is not a one-off. The Lhende Khola river system has now flooded twice in just 14 months and the increasingly unstable Himalayan ice system threatens communities, infrastructure and water supplies across one of the world’s most densely populated regions. The region saw similar flash floods in August last year, when a glacial lake in Tibet overflowed because of high temperatures. Nine people were killed, and critical infrastructure, including a bridge connecting Nepal and China, was damaged.

#tragedia  información  @laantenaoficial  —— #atencion #26Ago Nepal busca a cientos de desaparecidos tras una riada Al menos 55 personas murieron y 403 permanecen desaparecidas este miércoles después de que una riada repentina golpeara varias localidades cerca de la frontera con el Tíbet (China), según confirmaron las autoridades. El portavoz de la Policía de Nepal en la provincia de Bagmati, Rajendra Prasad Dhamala, elevó a 55 las personas fallecidas en el desastre que golpeó pueblos, mercados, carreteras y obras hidroeléctricas a primera hora de la mañana. Al mismo tiempo, la Junta de Turismo de Nepal aseguró que 403 personas, entre ellas 341 extranjeras, permanecen desaparecidas. Dos de ellas son de nacionalidad española, según las fuentes. El portavoz del Ejército de Nepal, Rajaram Basnet, declaró a EFE que al menos 29 personas habían sido rescatadas tras el desbordamiento del río Bhote Koshi. Basnet señaló que seis helicópteros del Ejército y otros ocho operados por empresas privadas fueron desplegados para las labores de búsqueda y rescate. “Es difícil evaluar los daños en este momento, pero es posible que tanto los daños como el número de víctimas sean considerables”, afirmó. La riada golpeó a primera hora del miércoles el distrito de Rasuwa, donde afectó pueblos, mercados, carreteras y obras hidroeléctricas e interrumpió el tránsito por una de las principales rutas terrestres entre Nepal y el Tíbet. La masa de agua llegó hacia las 9:15 hora local (3:30 GMT) al río Bhote Koshi desde la zona tibetana y golpeó con especial fuerza Timure, Rasuwagadhi y Syabrubesi, según fuentes oficiales. Las autoridades movilizaron a los cuerpos de seguridad y equipos de emergencia mientras trataban de determinar el alcance de los daños y localizar a las personas que permanecían sin contacto. Cada año, miles de personas viajan al monte Kailash y al lago Mansarovar, en el Tíbet, durante una peregrinación considerada sagrada por hindúes, budistas y jainistas. Nepal atribuye a un terremoto el origen de la riada El ministro de Asuntos Exteriores de Nepal, Shishir Khanal, afirmó este miércoles que la repentina riada que ha arrasado varias localidades  #nepal #tibet

🇳🇵 LOCAL SURVIVORS OF THE NEPAL FLOODS: THEY SURVIVED, BUT LOST ALMOST EVERYTHING For many local people, surviving the devastating floods was only the beginning of another struggle. 73-year-old Bhakta Lal Shrestha was at an elderly home in Devighat when the flood struck. He and more than 100 other residents were trapped for nearly nine hours before rescuers finally reached them. In Tupche village, 49-year-old Parbati Adhikari survived because she had left her village to visit a nearby temple before the flood arrived. When she tried to return, five bridges had already been washed away. She eventually found shelter with other survivors and was reunited with her husband and son. And 8-year-old Zoyal Ghale survived by running into the forest and climbing trees as floodwaters tore through his community. Injured and alone, he was eventually rescued and later reunited with his mother. These are more than numbers. They are mothers, fathers, children, grandparents and entire families who watched their homes disappear in minutes. Some survived. Some are still missing. And thousands of survivors are now facing the painful question: “Where do we go from here?” 🇳🇵💔 #NepalFloods #Nepal #FloodSurvivors #SurvivalStory #RescueMission

Nepal has been hit by a catastrophic flash flood disaster, beginning on 26 August 2026, particularly along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river corridors. 🇳🇵 What happened? The flooding was not simply ordinary monsoon flooding. A sudden ice/rock avalanche and collapse in the Himalayan region near Tibet caused a huge surge of water, mud, rocks and debris into the Bhote Koshi River. The resulting flash flood swept through villages and infrastructure with very little warning.  The worst-affected areas include Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading and Chitwan, with impacts also reported in Gorkha and Tanahun.  🕯️ Deaths and missing people The situation has continued to worsen as rescue teams recover bodies and update missing-person lists. As of 29–30 August, reports indicate more than 600 people have died in Nepal, with thousands still missing across Nepal and Tibet. AP reported 669 deaths in Nepal and nearly 3,000 people still missing as of August 30.  Many of the missing include foreign nationals, tourists, pilgrims and workers. 🚨 Rescue operation Nepalese security forces, helicopters and emergency teams are continuing search-and-rescue operations. More than 3,700 people have reportedly been rescued, while difficult mountain terrain, damaged roads and unstable conditions are making the operation extremely difficult.  A temporary lake formed near the disaster area also created fears of another flood, although the immediate risk has reportedly decreased as the lake has begun draining.  💔 Damage The floods have destroyed or severely damaged: Homes and entire villages Roads and bridges Hydropower plants Electricity infrastructure Border/trade infrastructure Health facilities Tourist and pilgrimage routes Nepal's government estimates that rebuilding could cost approximately US$4–5 billion.  The Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs has also been publishing official updates on the disaster and missing foreign nationals.  Important: Some dramatic videos circulating on Sri Lankan social media claiming to show the Nepal floods are actually old or unrelated footage, so they should not automatically be trusted.
